The Gospel Coalition
GOS-puhl koh-uh-LISH-uhn
noun (modern network)
Gospel from Old English gōdspel, good tidings; coalition from Latin coalescere, to grow together — a banding together around the gospel.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Gospel Coalition is a contemporary network of Reformed-leaning evangelicals founded in 2005 under the leadership of Timothy Keller and D. A. Carson, gathering pastors and writers around a shared confessional statement and a "gospel-centered" vision of ministry. This dictionary honors much in it: its written confession affirms the Trinity, the authority and inerrancy of Scripture, justification by faith alone, penal substitution, and salvation by grace; its theological vision presses for Christ-centered preaching that reads the whole Bible as pointing to the Redeemer (Luke 24:27); and its catechetical and reading resources have served many in the recovery of doctrine. It has labored to keep the gospel central where evangelicalism drifted toward moralism on one side and license on the other. Soberly, this dictionary notes the strains native to any broad-tent coalition: a confession framed to admit both Baptist and paedobaptist, both complementarian and the soft edges of the same, will at points speak less plainly than a full confession like the 1689, and a broad tent invites the pressures of the surrounding culture. These are concerns to weigh, not grievances to manufacture. This dictionary commends the Coalition's gospel-centered confession while measuring it, as all things, by the standard of the written Word.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A network of Reformed evangelicals founded in 2005 by Keller and Carson, centered on a gospel confession and Christ-centered preaching. Its confession is sound; the breadth of its coalition warrants sober watchfulness.

THE GOSPEL COALITION, noun. A contemporary evangelical network organized around a shared confession of the gospel and Reformed soteriology.

Founded 2005 under Timothy Keller and D. A. Carson.

"And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself" (Luke 24:27).

Affirms inerrancy, justification by faith alone, and penal substitution.

A broad coalition; its breadth is both its reach and the ground of sober watchfulness.

📖 Key Scripture

Luke 24:27 — "And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself."

1 Cor 15:3 — "For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;"

Gal 1:8 — "But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed."

Jude 1:3 — "Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The Gospel Coalition faces no postmodern redefinition; the watchfulness it warrants is the ordinary care owed to any broad-tent confession in a drifting culture.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The Coalition is a living evangelical body, not a contested term; the principle to recover is therefore measured discernment. Scripture commands that we "earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints" (Jude 3) and that we "prove all things; hold fast that which is good" (1 Thess 5:21). A confession framed to gather Baptists and paedobaptists under one roof will speak more generally than the 1689 on the sacraments and the church, and a wide platform is more exposed to the pressures of the age than a narrow pulpit.

Honesty requires naming both the good and the caution without overstatement. The good is real: a clear written gospel, Christ-centered exposition, sound men recovering Reformed truth for a new generation. The caution is ordinary: breadth dilutes precision, and broad coalitions must guard against cultural drift on the questions a generous statement leaves open. This dictionary commends the genuine service and confesses that every network, however sound its founding charter, stands or falls by the same Word it claims to honor — "to the law and to the testimony" (Isa 8:20).

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name joins gospel, the good tidings of Christ crucified, to coalition, a growing-together of churches around that message.

expand to see more

Gospel, Old English gōdspel, good news, rendering Greek euangelion.

Coalition, Latin coalescere, to grow together into one.

The name claims the gospel itself as the uniting center.

Its founding confession sets the boundaries of that union.

The breadth of the coalition is the chief object of sober watchfulness.

Usage

"The Gospel Coalition publishes articles, reviews, and reading plans for a wide readership."

"Many young Reformed pastors first encountered Christ-centered preaching through the Gospel Coalition."

"A confessional Baptist reads the Gospel Coalition with appreciation and measured discernment."
